tasks.name: Compare and contrast various types of security controls
Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security
Explain the importance of using appropriate cryptographic solutions

concepts.name: Security control categories
concepts.description: Distinguish technical, managerial, operational, and physical controls by how they are implemented.

concepts.name: Security control types
concepts.description: Distinguish preventive, deterrent, detective, corrective, compensating, and directive controls by their function.

concepts.name: CIA triad
concepts.description: Apply confidentiality, integrity, and availability to security scenarios.

concepts.name: Authentication, authorization, and accounting
concepts.description: Distinguish identity verification, permission decisions, and activity recording.

concepts.name: Non-repudiation
concepts.description: Recognize evidence and cryptographic mechanisms that make denial of a recorded action or signature difficult.

concepts.name: Gap analysis
concepts.description: Compare current and target security states to identify missing capabilities.

concepts.name: Zero Trust principles
concepts.description: Apply adaptive identity, threat-scope reduction, and policy-driven access without implicit trust based on network location.

concepts.name: Zero Trust logical components
concepts.description: Distinguish the Policy Engine, Policy Administrator, Policy Enforcement Point, control plane, and data plane.

concepts.name: Physical security
concepts.description: Recognize barriers, access controls, surveillance, lighting, and physical sensors.

concepts.name: Deception and disruption technology
concepts.description: Distinguish honeypots, honeynets, honeyfiles, and honeytokens.

concepts.name: Change-management workflow
concepts.description: Use ownership, stakeholders, testing, approval, maintenance windows, backout planning, and SOPs to make changes safely.

concepts.name: Change technical impact
concepts.description: Analyze allow/deny rules, downtime, restarts, legacy compatibility, restricted activities, and dependencies.

concepts.name: Change documentation and version control
concepts.description: Keep diagrams, policies, procedures, evidence, and version history aligned with the real environment.

concepts.name: Symmetric, asymmetric, and key exchange
concepts.description: Choose shared-secret encryption, public-key cryptography, or key establishment based on the requirement.

concepts.name: Encryption scope
concepts.description: Choose full-disk, partition/volume, file, database/record, or transport encryption at the right protection boundary.

concepts.name: Hashing, salting, and key stretching
concepts.description: Use cryptographic digests for integrity and salts/KDF cost for safer password storage.

concepts.name: Digital signatures
concepts.description: Use private-key signing and public-key verification for integrity, signer authentication, and non-repudiation support.

concepts.name: Public key infrastructure
concepts.description: Understand how PKI manages keys, certificate issuance, trust, validation, and revocation.

concepts.name: Certificate trust and status
concepts.description: Distinguish CAs, CSRs, self-signed and third-party certificates, wildcard names, CRLs, OCSP, and trust anchors.

concepts.name: Cryptographic key tools
concepts.description: Distinguish TPMs, HSMs, key management systems, and secure enclaves.

concepts.name: Algorithm, key length, and key escrow
concepts.description: Relate cryptographic strength to algorithm/key choices and recognize controlled key-recovery trade-offs.

concepts.name: Steganography, tokenization, and data masking
concepts.description: Distinguish different ways to conceal, substitute, or reduce exposure of sensitive data.

concepts.name: Blockchain and open public ledgers
concepts.description: Recognize cryptographically linked, independently verifiable ledger properties without assuming confidentiality.

questions.prompt: A monitoring system raises an alert after it observes repeated failed administrator logins. Which control type is the best fit?
questions.explanation: The control identifies suspicious activity and raises an alert, so its primary function is detective.
hints: If the control notices or reports an event, think detective.

choice_feedback.a: Correct. The control detects suspicious activity after it occurs and raises an alert.
choice_feedback.b: Preventive controls try to stop the event before it happens.
choice_feedback.c: Corrective controls restore or repair after a problem.
choice_feedback.d: Directive controls tell people what they must do.

questions.prompt: Place each control in the category that best describes how it is implemented.
questions.explanation: Technical controls are enforced by technology. Managerial controls guide governance and risk decisions. Operational controls are carried out through people and processes. Physical controls protect physical spaces or equipment.

questions.prompt: A storage service must encrypt a very large amount of data efficiently. Which cryptographic approach is normally the best fit for the bulk data itself?
questions.explanation: Symmetric encryption is normally preferred for bulk data because it is efficient. Public-key cryptography is often used for identity, signatures, or key establishment rather than encrypting every large data block.
hints: Bulk data plus efficiency should make you think symmetric.

choice_feedback.a: Correct. Symmetric encryption is normally the efficient choice for bulk data.
choice_feedback.b: Public-key operations are much more expensive and are usually used for signatures, identity, or key establishment rather than every data block.
choice_feedback.c: Hashing checks integrity; it does not encrypt the data.
choice_feedback.d: A digital signature provides integrity/authenticity evidence, not confidentiality.

steps.prompt: The update breaks production. What should the team do?

choices.label: Continue the rollout despite the failure
Wait for users to find a workaround

choice_feedback.a: Correct. Compatibility testing, impact analysis, and a recovery path reduce the chance of a security change causing an outage.
choice_feedback.b: Security and availability both matter. A stronger setting does not justify an untested production outage.
choice_feedback.c: A maintenance window limits timing risk but does not replace compatibility testing.
choice_feedback.d: Removing the previous configuration destroys a recovery option.

questions.prompt: A team documents assumptions about a self-signed server certificate. Select every faulty assumption.
questions.explanation: A self-signed certificate can contain a public key and can participate in encrypted communication. The key trust issue is identity assurance: a new client does not automatically have a trusted third-party CA chain or trust anchor for that certificate.
hints: Separate encryption capability from how the client establishes identity trust.

elements.label: The certificate can contain a public key

choice_feedback.b: A self-signed certificate still contains a public key.
choice_feedback.c: A self-signed certificate can still be used with encrypted TLS; the issue is trust, not whether encryption is possible.
choice_feedback.d: Self-signing does not create automatic trust on other systems.

hints: Think tamper evidence, not automatic secrecy.

elements.label: Move to an approved modern algorithm with an appropriate key length
Keep a fundamentally broken algorithm as long as the key is made longer
Replace encryption with data masking because masking is always cryptographically stronger
Use a shorter key because shorter keys are always harder to attack

choice_feedback.a: Correct. A broken or obsolete algorithm must be replaced; key length alone cannot repair a fundamental weakness.
choice_feedback.b: Adding a tiny amount of key length does not make an obsolete algorithm safe.
choice_feedback.c: Masking is not a replacement for cryptographic encryption.
choice_feedback.d: Shorter keys generally reduce brute-force resistance rather than increase it.
